records.Concise description: A deployed Bitcoin peer-to-peer transport specification adding opportunistic encrypted v2 connections, pseudorandom wire encoding, and transport-version extensibility.
records.Deeper researched summary: BIP 324 defines Bitcoin's version-2 P2P transport. It raises the cost of passive observation and some network attacks by encrypting traffic opportunistically and making the byte stream less self-identifying, while remaining compatible with fallback to v1 peers. The protocol does not provide authenticated peer identities by itself, so 'encrypted' must not be simplified to 'authenticated' or 'private.' The BIP is marked Deployed and its specification was updated in 2026.
records.Launch / history: Assigned in 2019, finalized in 2024, and marked Deployed. The published specification received clarifying updates in January and July 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the most important modern changes to Bitcoin's transport layer and cleanly demonstrates the difference between transport security, P2P application messages, node policy, and consensus.
records.Verification basis: Primary BIP specification was checked and is marked Deployed, with version history updated through July 2026.
Research notes / uncertainties: BIP 324 provides opportunistic encryption, not authenticated peer identity or guaranteed anonymity.
Deployment is implementation/configuration dependent; 'deployed' does not mean every Bitcoin connection uses v2 transport.

records.Entity / project type: specialized low-latency block-relay network / Bitcoin Core patchset
records.Concise description: A specialized low-latency Bitcoin block-relay system using a Bitcoin Core patchset, UDP, forward-error correction, and Compact Blocks.
records.Deeper researched summary: FIBRE—the Fast Internet Bitcoin Relay Engine—was created as the successor to the Bitcoin Relay Network to reduce block-propagation latency, especially for miners and geographically distributed block producers. Its specialized nodes trade some denial-of-service resistance for speed by forwarding data before full validation, while external Bitcoin nodes still need normal validation. After years of stasis, Localhost Research revived maintenance in 2025 and now operates a public FIBRE network. FIBRE complements rather than replaces the public Bitcoin P2P network.
Creators / founders: w0xlt and Justin / Localhost Research — maintenance revival from 2025
records.Launch / history: Designed and operated in 2016–2017, then largely dormant for years. Maintenance was taken over by Localhost Research in 2025, which operates an active public network in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is historically and currently important specialized relay infrastructure for minimizing block propagation delay and the stale-block advantage of well-connected or geographically favored miners.
records.Verification basis: Current official FIBRE site documents the 2025 maintenance revival, Localhost Research public network, architecture, and relay/validation tradeoffs.
Research notes / uncertainties: FIBRE is not a replacement for Bitcoin's public P2P network.
FIBRE relays specialized data before full validation for latency; downstream nodes must still independently validate blocks.
Do not convert vendor/operator claims about stale-rate effects into universal measured guarantees.

records.Concise description: Matt Corallo's 2014–2016 specialized relay network for faster block propagation, the direct predecessor to FIBRE.
records.Deeper researched summary: The Bitcoin Relay Network used globally distributed relay nodes and a fast custom relay path to reduce block-propagation delay for miners and well-connected Bitcoin nodes. Its own documentation emphasized that it did not replace the public Bitcoin P2P network and that relayed data still required full validation before mining on it. The network was superseded by FIBRE as Compact Blocks and forward-error-correction techniques enabled a better design.
records.Launch / history: Operated primarily from 2014 to 2016 and then gave way to FIBRE, which incorporated lessons from the earlier relay network.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It documents an important shift in Bitcoin networking: specialized relay infrastructure emerged to reduce block propagation latency, then evolved into FIBRE rather than becoming part of consensus.
Important technical or cultural characte: Full validation still required by recipients
records.Verification basis: Historical first-party Relay Network site plus current FIBRE history establish the 2014–2016 role and supersession.
Research notes / uncertainties: Historical only; do not present old relay endpoints or topology as active.
The relay network never removed the need for recipient validation.
